ops.text:
ccx vcs ship refuses in a repo whose trunk is unambiguous to any human, because a
worktree-* bookmark left by a workflow-isolated agent pollutes trunk resolution.

Hit during the 48-move fleet sweep (2026-07-30), on cc-notes:

  ccx: ship: cannot resolve the trunk bookmark from ["main" "worktree-wf_6f0707d4-36b-1"]; pass --branch naming one of them

The two candidates are `main` and `worktree-wf_6f0707d4-36b-1` — the latter created by
Claude Code's WorktreeCreate hook for an agent worktree, sitting on the same commit as
main. It is LIVE (checked out in another worktree, `+` in git branch -vv), so deleting it
is not the workaround: it would pull a branch out from under a running session.

Two things make this sharper than a generic ambiguity error:

1. `ccx vcs restack` resolves trunk on its own path and fails the same way, but a sweep
   that gates restack on "is the repo behind?" never reaches it. cc-notes was current with
   origin/main, so restack was correctly skipped — and ship then refused anyway. Guarding
   the restack path does not guard the ship path.

2. The bookmark is not junk to be cleaned up. Agent worktrees are created and destroyed
   continuously by the harness, so any repo running workflow-isolated agents can acquire a
   worktree-* bookmark on its trunk commit at any moment. A repo that ships fine at 10:00
   can refuse at 10:05 with no user action.

Reproduction: in a colocated jj repo, create a bookmark alongside `main` pointing at the
same commit (`jj bookmark create worktree-wf_test -r main`), then run `ccx vcs ship`.
`ccx vcs info` shows the ambiguity as `branch  main worktree-wf_test`.

Candidate fixes, none obviously right: prefer the tracked bookmark when exactly one of the
candidates has a remote counterpart; ignore `worktree-*` when resolving trunk; or fall back
to trunk() rather than erroring when the candidates all point at the same commit.
Related but distinct: task 706d5d1 covers an UNTRACKED main@origin, not multiple bookmarks.
